title: ScrumIA — compose your AI dev team from replaceable Claude Code modules
meta_description: A method and a marketplace of Claude Code plugins to run a project with AI agents: specs, tickets, standing roles, coding practices. Every module can be swapped.
og_title: ScrumIA — compose your AI dev team
hero_lead: Scoping, specs, tickets, code, reviews — fill each slot with a Claude Code plugin, and swap it the day the project changes.
hero_hop_alt: Hop, the ScrumIA mascot: four flow-diagram columns gathered into a body, one eye lit.
flow_title: Seven steps. Three of them are you.
flow_intro: One idea, from a sentence to a merged pull request. Three of its seven steps wait for a person; the other four run without one.
flow1_out: An idea, a problem. Nothing formatted.
flow3_out: Each role weighs in.→ Ready for dev
flow4_out: Only on doubt, risk or criticality.
flow6_out: One worktree each.→ spec, code, PR
flow7_out: You read it and test.→ Done
legend_swap: Swap a module and this line changes shape.
you1_desc: You state the problem. The agents challenge it; you settle what blocks them.
you2_desc: Only on designs that are doubtful, critical or risky. The rest just ships.
you3_desc: The final call stays yours, unless you delegate it in writing.
slots_intro: A slot is a question. A module is one answer. Below is this repo's real composition, read from .scrumia/config.yaml — two of the seven are empty, and nothing is faked in their place.
slot_specs_q: Where do specs live, in what shape?
slot_specs_a: One directory per feature, files created only when they have something to say, acceptance criteria written first and turned into tests.
slot_tracker_q: Where does state live — tickets, columns, PRs?
slot_tracker_a: GitHub Issues and Projects. Nothing stateful in the repo, and a hook that refuses the commit which tries.
slot_team_q: Which standing roles, with what scope?
slot_team_a: Manager, business, tech — plus a designer contributed by the design module. Each boundary is a line of refusal, and every role toggles by config.
slot_discovery_q: How does an idea become scoped work?
slot_discovery_a: scrumia-discovery is installed here. An idea gets a scoping pass before it becomes a ticket: scrumia-brainstorm opens the question, scrumia-split cuts what comes out of it into issues.
slot_impl_q: How is code written, per app?
slot_impl_a: This product ships markdown. Its two code apps — a static site and a validation script — carry no implementation module, so the instruction is to follow the neighbouring code instead of inventing a doctrine.
slot_practices_a: None here. TDD, SOLID and TanStack Query are on the shelf — a repository of prose doesn't need them, and pretending otherwise would cost every agent context it could spend on the work.
slot_design_q: Where does the design system live?
slot_design_a: Identity, tokens and components as files in the repo, synced one at a time with a Claude Design project. A value the tokens don't carry is a finding, not an exception — including on this page.
comp_intro: Seven slots, seven decisions — including the ones you leave empty on purpose. Same index as above, except here you answer it: the rows write your install commands and the .scrumia/config.yaml that scrumia-init verifies.
comp_specs_d: One directory per feature, files created only when they have something to say, acceptance criteria written before the code.
comp_specs_empty: No specs contract: agents work a ticket from its own text, skip spec updates, and say so. What was decided survives only where the ticket happened to write it down.
comp_specs_yaml: # no specs contract — agents work from the ticket text
comp_tracker_d: Issues, board columns and PRs on GitHub. Nothing stateful in the repo, and a hook that refuses the commit which tries.
comp_tracker_own: Jira, Linear, anything else. The slot has a defined contract, so the module is bounded work — until it exists the slot is empty and behaves as such.
comp_tracker_own_yaml: # no tracker module yet — yours to write; until it exists, ticket and board skills degrade to text
comp_tracker_empty: Ticket, board and review skills degrade to text output, and say so. Project state has nowhere to live: no columns, no PR routing, no record of what is in flight.
comp_tracker_yaml: # no tracker — ticket and board skills degrade to text
comp_team_d: Manager, business and tech as standing roles — each with a scope, a model, and a line of refusal.
comp_team_empty: No standing roles: nothing challenges a business rule, an architecture choice or a screen before merge, and nothing batches a sprint. Every verdict falls back to you.
comp_team_yaml: # no standing roles — every verdict is yours
comp_discovery_d: A scoping pass between an idea and a ticket: challenge it, split it into features, write the specs on a branch.
comp_discovery_empty: An idea goes straight to a ticket without a scoping pass, and the agents are told to say so instead of improvising one.
comp_discovery_yaml: # no discovery — an idea goes straight to a ticket
comp_impl_empty: Empty: agents follow the neighbouring code — normal behaviour, not a gap. The cost arrives with the first file of a new stack, where there is no neighbour to follow.
comp_practices_empty: Empty: no cross-cutting discipline is imposed. Nothing makes tests come first or keeps a pattern consistent across apps — what the implementation module does not say, nobody says.
comp_design_d: Identity, tokens and components as files in the repo, plus a designer role that judges what a user actually sees.
comp_design_empty: No design contract: each page is styled by taste, values go inline with no token to answer for them, and no role judges the interface before merge.
comp_design_yaml: # no design contract — no role judges the interface
comp_app_empty_yaml: # no module of its own — agents follow the code next to it
comp_out_config_role: commit it, then scrumia-init verifies it instead of asking again
comp_c_then: # then, inside the repo to set up
comp_c_config: # Generated by the composer — review, then commit
comp_note_own_tracker: The tracker slot has a defined contract, so writing a Jira or Linear module is bounded work. Until it exists, the ticket and board skills degrade to text output and say so.
comp_note_own_impl: No implementation module for that stack: the app follows the conventions of the code next to it. Normal behaviour, not a gap — and the contract for writing your own fits on one page.
comp_note_practices: Practices apply app by app, and only to the app types they speak for. Where one disagrees with the implementation module, the implementation module wins.
comp_note_practices_noapp: Practices attach to apps. With no app declared they install and activate nothing until apps appear in the file.
comp_impl_rust_d: Typed errors, invariants, one test per invariant.
comp_impl_other_d: Follows the neighbouring code — or write your module.
comp_practice_tdd_d: Red-green-refactor, audit and refactor skills included.
comp_practice_tanstack_d: Query keys, invalidation, optimistic updates — the server/client boundary.
ext_claim: A skill declares where it can be extended; any module answers, and nothing is stored — so nothing goes stale.
ext_fact1: A skill opens a register without naming who will fill it.
ext_fact2_a: Any installed module can contribute to it without naming the skill back — here,
ext_fact3_a: A register can carry no contribution at all, and that is a normal state, not a gap — here,
ext_ask: Ask, and this project's own composition answers:
ext_outro: The table above is not read from anywhere: it was computed the moment you asked, so it cannot go stale. This is what can be added without replacing anything — see Slots for what can be replaced instead. Writing a contribution of your own is the reference's job, not this page's.
mods_intro: Twelve shipped. Each is a standard Claude Code plugin — install what you need.
mod_core_d: Describes the active composition and writes it into CLAUDE.md. Fills no slot.
mod_rules_d: Rule sections a project can own: index, guides, decisions — no rule without its why.
mod_specs_d: Per-feature specs, TDD-oriented. A file catalog instead of one document.
mod_ghp_d: Issues, sub-issues, Projects columns, branches and PRs. Requires gh.
mod_teams_d: Standing roles and sprint execution in dynamic workflows. Roles are configurable.
mod_disc_d: Challenges an idea until it can be split, then ships specs on a branch.
mod_rust_d: Invalid states unrepresentable, typed errors per layer, one test per invariant — plus an audit skill for existing code.
mod_solidjs_d: Fine-grained reactivity without React reflexes, behaviour-first component tests — plus an audit skill.
mod_tdd_d: The cycle operationalized for an agent, the mock boundary, AC-to-test mapping. Reference, audit, refactor.
mod_solid_d: The five principles, each with its limit. Audits violations and over-applications alike. Reference, audit, refactor.
mod_tanstack_d: Query keys, options, mutations, testing — 9 guides, 13 decisions, ported from real monorepo use.
mod_design_d: Identity, tokens and components in the repo, synced one at a time with Claude Design. Ships the designer role and an audit that reports drift and mutedness alike.
install_prereq: Prerequisites: git, an authenticated gh CLI (for the GitHub tracker), and jq (for the guard hook). scrumia-init checks all three and says what degrades if one is missing.

install_after: scrumia-init maps your apps, proposes a composition, offers the install command for each module it needs, and writes the composition into CLAUDE.md. Re-running it checks instead of overwriting.
